mainTopic: Why משניות give numbers, and the source that each ערוה brings a separate liability
overview: The גמרא asks why our משנה says 'thirty-six כריתות' when it lists them all anyway. רבי יוחנן answers that the number teaches a separate חטאת for each sin done in one הֶעְלֵם, and the same holds for the thirty-nine אבות מלאכות of שבת. The גמרא then runs through other משניות that give numbers. Most of these numbers reject another תנא's list, such as רבי אליעזר בן יעקב on the גר, רבי שמעון on שבועת הפקדון, רבי אליעזר on the נשיא, and the chain of counts for אבות נזיקין. The count of five who bring one קרבן for many sins shows the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about when a טמא נזיר's pure נזירות restarts. Next, the גמרא returns to רבי יוחנן and asks how we know each ערוה is a separate liability. He answers from the separate כרת for the sister, and after רב ביבי בר אביי's challenge, a הקש ties all the עריות to her. Finally, the גמרא shows how רבי יצחק and the רבנן each find sources for separate liability, and this discussion continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why does the משנה give a number?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say 'thirty-six' when it lists every case anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why our משנה bothers to say there are thirty-six כריתות. Anyone could count the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names every case that brings כרת, so the number looks extra. The גמרא assumes the משנה does not waste words. If the number is there, it must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: A number or count given in the משנה
Why do I need it? (asks what a word or detail adds)
Being cut off, the heavenly punishment for certain sins done on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether the count of thirty-six is correct. It is asking why the משנה states a number at all when the full list is right there.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why do I need the number?
phrases.notes: He means the opening words of our משנה, 'thirty-six כריתות are in the Torah,' which come before the full list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the first words of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra lesson does the number thirty-six teach, since the list already shows it?

steps.title: The number teaches a separate liability for each sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the number teaches that someone who did all thirty-six in one הֶעְלֵם is liable for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It teaches that if someone did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that the number tells us how many separate obligations a person can have. If he did all the sins while unaware, he owes one for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one הֶעְלֵם (one period of not knowing) joins repeated acts into a single חטאת. The number thirty-six shows that different sins do not join together. Each one counts on its own, so a person could owe thirty-six חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: One lapse of awareness: a single stretch of time in which the person did not know or forgot
Liable for each and every one (a separate obligation for each sin)
Sin offering, brought for doing by accident a sin that brings כרת when done on purpose

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the pattern for the next steps. A number in a משנה can teach how many separate obligations there are.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
That if one did all of them in one lapse of awareness
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁאִם עֲשָׂאָן כּוּלָּן בְּהֶעְלֵם אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number teaches that each of the thirty-six sins brings its own חטאת, even if all were done in one הֶעְלֵם.

steps.title: The same question about the thirty-nine labors of שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the משנה in שבת that says there are 'forty minus one' main labors.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, that which we learned: 'The main categories of labor are forty minus one.' Why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another משנה that gives a number, the list of labors forbidden on שבת. It asks again why the number is needed. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like our משנה, the משנה in שבת lists every labor, so the count 'forty minus one' again looks extra. The גמרא raises the same question to see if the same answer works.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (brings up another similar case)
The main categories of labor forbidden on שבת
Forty minus one, meaning thirty-nine

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which we learned:
The main categories of labor are forty minus one,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שבת 73a.

phrases.english: why do I need the number?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, הָא דִּתְנַן: אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the question of step 1 to a parallel משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the count of thirty-nine add in the משנה of שבת?

steps.title: Same answer: a separate חטאת for each labor
steps.stepSummary: The number teaches that someone who did all thirty-nine labors in one הֶעְלֵם brings a חטאת for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: That if someone did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as רבי יוחנן's. The number thirty-nine teaches that each main labor brings its own חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who did many labors on שבת without knowing it was forbidden does not get one combined חטאת. Each אב מלאכה is a separate sin, so he could owe up to thirty-nine.

keyTerms.meaning: He did them
All of them
A main category of labor (the singular of אבות מלאכות)

steps.whatToRemember: A number in a משנה can teach that the items do not join together. Each item brings its own חטאת, even in one הֶעְלֵם.

phrases.english: That if one did all of them in one lapse of awareness
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 using the same reasoning as step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count of thirty-nine teaches a separate חטאת for each אב מלאכה done in one הֶעְלֵם.

steps.title: The same question about the four people still missing atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says there are 'four' מחוסרי כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, that which we learned: 'Four are missing atonement.' Why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the question a third time, now about the משנה that lists four people who still need an offering before they may eat קדשים. This sets up a new kind of answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the answer from before does not fit. These people are not sinners who owe a חטאת for each act. So the number must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: People still missing atonement: they finished their purification but must bring an offering before they may eat קדשים
Atonement, here the offering that completes purification
Four

phrases.english: Furthermore, that which we learned:
Four are missing atonement,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 8b of our מסכת, which lists the זב, the זבה, the woman after childbirth, and the מצורע.

phrases.english: why do I need the number?

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוּ, הָא דִּתְנַן: אַרְבָּעָה מְחוּסְּרֵי כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question to a third משנה that gives a number
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the count of four add in the list of מחוסרי כפרה?

steps.title: The number four rejects a view that counts five
steps.stepSummary: The number is there to reject רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says there are five מחוסרי כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to exclude the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who said there are five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. Saying 'four' rules out רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view that there are five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is different from the first two. There the number taught separate liability. Here it shuts out another תנא's longer list: only four, no more.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to rule out (another opinion)
Five
There are

steps.confusionAlert: Do not carry over the earlier answer. Here the number is not about a separate offering for each item. It rejects a different opinion about who belongs on the list.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
who said: There are five,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 with a different reason than steps 2 and 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number four rejects רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who counts five מחוסרי כפרה.

steps.title: The source showing רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds the convert
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב counts the גר as a fifth מחוסר כפרה, and that is why the משנה says four.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: A convert is missing atonement until blood is sprinkled for him. That is why the משנה teaches four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the fifth one is a גר. It then concludes that this is why our משנה says 'four'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a גר is like the others on the list. He may not eat קדשים until the blood of his offering is sprinkled on the מזבח. Our משנה says 'four' on purpose to leave the גר off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
Until the blood (of his offering) is sprinkled for him
For this reason it taught

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for a number in a משנה. Sometimes it teaches a separate חטאת for each item (כריתות, מלאכות). Sometimes it rejects another opinion that has more items (four מחוסרי כפרה, not five).

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught, Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
A convert is missing atonement
until blood is sprinkled for him,
for this reason it taught four.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: גֵּר מְחוּסַּר כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא behind the opinion mentioned in step 6 and closes the answer
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר בן יעקב counts five מחוסרי כפרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where he includes the גר until the blood of his offering is sprinkled
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה says 'four' to leave out the גר and reject רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's count of five.

steps.title: Why does the משנה count 'four' who bring a קרבן even for an on-purpose sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the same pattern going and asks why the משנה needs the number 'four' in its list of sins where a זדון is treated like a שגגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, the משנה says: four people bring a קרבן for doing the sin on purpose, just as for doing it by mistake. Why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks its next 'why the number?' question, this time about a different list in the משנה. It is setting up an answer that will explain what the number 'four' adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a חטאת or אשם is brought only for a mistake (שגגה), not for an on-purpose sin (זדון). The משנה lists four exceptions where even a זדון gets a קרבן. Just listing them would be enough, so the גמרא asks what the number itself teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing a sin on purpose
Doing a sin by mistake
Why do I need the number?
Furthermore, also

phrases.english: Furthermore, that which we learned:
Four bring an offering for the on-purpose sin just as for the mistaken one,
phrases.notes: The four are: one who lives with a שפחה חרופה, a נזיר who became טמא, a false oath about testimony, and a false oath about a deposit.

phrases.english: why do I need the number?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same 'why the number?' question, now applied to a new list in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the number 'four' add beyond the list itself?

steps.title: The number four rejects רבי שמעון about the deposit oath
steps.stepSummary: The number 'four' is there to reject רבי שמעון, who holds that someone who swears falsely about a deposit on purpose cannot bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי שמעון. A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, for a false oath about a deposit, the on-purpose sinner is not given atonement through a קרבן. That is why the משנה says four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the number is there to reject רבי שמעון's view, and quotes a ברייתא to show what רבי שמעון holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that שבועת הפקדון done on purpose does not get a קרבן, so he would count only three. By writing 'four', the משנה makes it clear that the deposit oath belongs in the list. This works just like the earlier answer about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the number of מחוסרי כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to reject (a different view)
A false oath denying that one holds someone else's deposit
Atonement
For this reason

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the number in the משנה can quietly take a side in a מחלוקת between תנאים.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Shimon,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Shimon says:
The oath about a deposit:
its on-purpose version is not given atonement,
For this reason the משנה teaches 'four'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number 'four' rejects רבי שמעון, who would not count the on-purpose deposit oath, and so would have only three.

steps.title: Why does the משנה count 'five' who bring one קרבן for many sins?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the number 'five' in its list of people who bring one קרבן for many sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, the משנה says: five people bring one קרבן for many sins. Why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same 'why the number?' question about yet another list. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה lists five people who bring only one קרבן even if they did the same thing many times. Again, the list could stand without a number, so the גמרא asks what the number 'five' adds.

keyTerms.meaning: One offering
Many sins (the same thing done many times)

phrases.english: Furthermore, that which we learned:
Five bring one offering
phrases.notes: The five are: a man with a שפחה חרופה many times, a נזיר who became טמא many times, a husband who warned his wife about many men, a מצורע with many afflictions, and a woman who gave birth many times.

phrases.english: for many sins,
why do I need the number?

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוּ, הָא דִּתְנַן: חֲמִשָּׁה מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same pattern of question again, now about the list of five.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the number 'five' add beyond the list itself?

steps.title: The number five makes sure the נזיר case is counted
steps.stepSummary: The number is there because the משנה wants to include the case of a נזיר who became טמא many times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wants to teach the later part: a נזיר who became טמא many times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the number 'five' is there to make sure the נזיר who became טמא many times is part of the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the number makes sure we count a case that is unusual and hard to picture: the נזיר who became טמא many times. The next steps explain how that case can happen. They also show that it only works according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and not according to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה
A person who took a vow of נזירות
Many separate cases of becoming טמא

phrases.english: Because he wants to teach the later part:
a נזיר, if he became טמא many times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number makes sure the unusual case of the נזיר who became טמא many times is counted among the five.

steps.title: How a נזיר can become טמא many separate times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes the case: the נזיר became טמא on the seventh day, and then became טמא again on the seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you can find this case where he became טמא on the seventh day, and then became טמא again on the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the נזיר case in the משנה actually looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a נזיר became טמא again while he was still in his seven days of purification, it would all just be one טומאה. So the case must be that he finished his purification on the seventh day and then became טמא again on a seventh day. Each one counts as a separate טומאה, and still the משנה says one קרבן is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it (this is how the case happens)
The seventh day of the purification process

steps.confusionAlert: 'The seventh' here is the seventh day of the נזיר's purification after becoming טמא, not the seventh day of his נזירות.

phrases.english: And you can find this
where he became טמא on the seventh day
and became טמא again on the seventh day,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the נזיר case mentioned in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is a נזיר who became טמא on the seventh day and became טמא again on a seventh day.

steps.title: This follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this case follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds that the new נזירות of purity starts from the seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says that the נזירות of purity starts for him from the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view the case follows and answers: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the נזיר's new, pure נזירות already starts on the seventh day, even before he brings his קרבנות on the eighth. So a טומאה on the seventh day counts as a brand new טומאה of his נזירות. That is why becoming טמא on the seventh day and then again on the seventh day can be many separate טומאות.

keyTerms.meaning: And whose view is it?
The new, pure נזירות he keeps after becoming טהור
Takes effect, starts

steps.whatToRemember: Each number in these משניות has a job: 'four' rejects רבי שמעון about the deposit oath, and 'five' makes sure the unusual נזיר case is counted. That נזיר case follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says the pure נזירות starts on the seventh day.

phrases.english: And whose view is it?
It is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: the נזירות of purity
takes effect on him from the seventh day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַנִּי? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names whose view the case in step 12 follows and explains why the case works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, for whom the pure נזירות starts on the seventh day, so a טומאה on that day counts as a new one.

steps.title: According to רבי, the case cannot happen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the case must follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. According to רבי, pure נזירות only starts on the eighth day, so how could this case of many separate טומאות ever happen?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the משנה follows רבי, there is a problem. He holds that pure נזירות does not start until the eighth day. So how could you ever find this case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a test. It asks whether the case from step 12 could work according to רבי, and suggests it could not. The next steps check both possible ways the case could happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a נזיר becomes טמא, he purifies himself for seven days and brings קרבנות on the eighth. Then he starts his נזירות again in purity. רבי holds that the new pure נזירות only 'takes hold' on the eighth day. That makes it hard to build a case of many separate טומאות that still need only one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The נזיר's new count of נזירות in a state of purity, after he has finished purifying himself
Takes effect, starts to apply
How can you find it? Meaning: how could this case ever happen?

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' means a specific person: רבי יהודה הנשיא. It is not a general title for some rabbi.

phrases.english: For if you say it is the opinion of Rebbi,
phrases.notes: This 'רבי' is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: since the naziriteship of purity
does not take effect on him until the eighth day,
how can you find this case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 13's claim by showing that the other opinion, רבי's, cannot produce the case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה's case could follow רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי, pure נזירות only starts on the eighth day, so there seems to be no way to have many separate טומאות that are all covered by one קרבן.

steps.title: Becoming impure again on the seventh day is one long impurity
steps.stepSummary: Option one: the נזיר became טמא on the seventh day again and again. According to רבי, this is all one long טומאה, not many separate ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became impure on the seventh day, and then became impure again on the seventh day, it is all one long impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first way the case could happen and rejects it according to רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the נזיר never reached the eighth day, so his pure נזירות never restarted between the two טומאות. That means it is really one long טומאה. Then there is nothing special about bringing only one קרבן, and it is not a case of 'many' טומאות.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh day of the purification process, the day the נזיר shaves
One long, stretched-out impurity, as opposed to separate impurities
And he again became impure

phrases.english: If he became impure on the seventh day
and again became impure on the seventh day,
it is all one long impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּנִטְמָא בִּשְׁבִיעִי וְחָזַר וְנִטְמָא בִּשְׁבִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible version of the case raised in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The seventh-day version of the case, according to רבי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For רבי, the pure נזירות never restarted, so the two טומאות merge into one long טומאה.

steps.title: Becoming impure again on the eighth day needs a separate offering each time
steps.stepSummary: Option two: the נזיר became טמא on the eighth day each time. Since he already reached a time when he could bring his קרבן, he must bring a separate קרבן for each טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became impure on the eighth day, and again on the eighth day, he is obligated for each one. That is because he came out of his impurity at a time fit for bringing a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second way the case could happen and rejects it too, because here the law would be a separate קרבן for each טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reaching the eighth day means the נזיר had a proper moment to bring his קרבן. That closes off the first טומאה as its own event. So each טומאה needs its own קרבן, which does not fit a משנה that says one קרבן covers many sins.

keyTerms.meaning: A time fit for something, here a time when he could properly bring his קרבן
Obligated for each and every one, so a separate קרבן for each
The eighth day, the day the נזיר brings his קרבנות

phrases.english: And if he became impure on the eighth day
and again became impure on the eighth day,
since he came out at a time that is fit
for bringing a קרבן,
he is obligated for each and every one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי דְּנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁמִינִי וְחָזַר וְנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁמִינִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible version of the case after step 15 rejected the first.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The eighth-day version of the case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reaching a time fit for a קרבן separates the טומאות, so each needs its own קרבן.

steps.title: So the case follows רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since the case cannot work according to רבי, the משנה must follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof. Both options failed for רבי, so the case must follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the new pure נזירות starts on the seventh day. So a second טומאה on the seventh day is a real new טומאה. But he never reached the eighth day, the time fit for a קרבן, so one קרבן covers them all. This confirms step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the גמרא's way of saying 'this proves'

steps.whatToRemember: The case of the נזיר who becomes טמא again and again on the seventh day, yet brings one קרבן, only works for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. For him, pure נזירות restarts on the seventh day, but the time for the קרבן is the eighth.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this
that it is the opinion of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after steps 15 and 16 ruled out both options for רבי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's count of 'five', which includes the נזיר case, follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: What are the two opinions based on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the opinions of רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the opinion of רבי, and what is the opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the argument it has been using. This sets up the ברייתא quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא assumed the two opinions about when pure נזירות starts. Now it wants to see where in the sources this argument actually appears.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Here it means: what is this opinion, and where is it found?

phrases.english: What is the opinion of Rebbi,
and what is the opinion of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי וּמַאי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the two opinions used in steps 13 through 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the argument about when pure נזירות begins again

steps.title: The verse 'he shall sanctify his head that day'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'וקדש את ראשו ביום ההוא' in two ways. רבי says it means the day of the קרבנות, the eighth. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it means the day of shaving, the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall sanctify his head that day' means the day he brings his קרבנות, says רבי. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it means the day he shaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא where the two sages argue over which day the פסוק is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Sanctify his head' means the נזיר starts his holy נזירות again. רבי says this happens on the day of the קרבנות, the eighth. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it happens on the day of shaving, the seventh. This is the root of the whole argument used above.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall sanctify his head, meaning he starts his נזירות again
On that day; the two sages argue about which day this is
The bringing of his קרבנות (the eighth day)
His shaving (the seventh day)

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument over one phrase in the פסוק decides when the טמא נזיר's new pure נזירות begins. That is the reason the משנה's count of 'five' has to follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And he shall sanctify his head that day":
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:11

phrases.english: on the day he brings his offerings,
these are the words of Rebbi.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
on the day of his shaving.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְקִדַּשׁ אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument comes from במדבר 6:11. רבי reads 'that day' as the day of the קרבנות (eighth). רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads it as the day of shaving (seventh).

steps.title: Why does the משנה count five who bring a sliding-scale offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says 'five' people bring a קרבן עולה ויורד, when it could just list them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, there is the משנה that says: 'Five bring a קרבן עולה ויורד.' Why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its series of questions and picks another משנה that gives a number. It asks why the number is needed, and this sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the five cases anyway, so the count seems to add nothing. The גמרא assumes a number in a משנה always comes to teach something. So it looks for what this count is coming to rule out.

keyTerms.meaning: Furthermore; one more case
A sliding-scale offering: a rich person brings an animal, a poorer person brings birds, a very poor person brings flour
Why do I need the number?

phrases.english: Furthermore, that which we learned in a משנה:
Five bring a sliding-scale offering,
phrases.notes: These five are: hearing an oath, a false spoken oath, טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, a woman after birth, and a מצורע.

phrases.english: why do I need the number?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with the נזיר example, the גמרא goes on to another משנה that gives a number.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the count of 'five' add to the list of those who bring a קרבן עולה ויורד?

steps.title: The number five rejects רבי אליעזר's view about the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The count is there because of the rule about the נשיא. It comes to reject רבי אליעזר, who says a נשיא brings a fixed goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because another משנה later teaches: 'The נשיא is like them.' The word 'five' comes to reject רבי אליעזר, who says a נשיא brings a goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the number 'five' is there to push away רבי אליעזר's opinion about a נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that for at least one of these sins a נשיא brings a fixed goat, not a sliding-scale offering. By saying 'five', the משנה makes the list one fixed group with no special exception for a נשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה
The king or Jewish ruler
To exclude; to reject another opinion
A goat; here a fixed חטאת, not a sliding-scale offering

phrases.english: Because the later clause teaches:
The נשיא is like them.
phrases.notes: This line is quoted from a משנה in הוריות that deals with the נשיא and these sliding-scale sins.

phrases.english: The 'five' is to exclude the view of רבי אליעזר,
who says: a נשיא brings a goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count of five rejects רבי אליעזר, who holds that a נשיא brings a fixed goat instead of a sliding-scale offering.
steps.whatToRemember: A number in a משנה is often there to reject another תנא's opinion.

steps.title: Why does the משנה count four main types of damage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the opening משנה of בבא קמא says 'four' אבות נזיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, there is the משנה that says: 'There are four main categories of damage.' Why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more משנה that gives a number and asks what the number adds. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same pattern as before: the משנה names the categories anyway, so why count them? The גמרא looks for the opinion that the number rejects.

keyTerms.meaning: The main categories of damage a person is responsible for

phrases.english: Furthermore, that which we learned in a משנה:
There are four main categories of damage,
phrases.notes: This is the first משנה in בבא קמא: the ox, the pit, the מבעה, and fire.

phrases.english: why do I need the number?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next example in the series of 'why the number' questions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the count of 'four' add to the list of אבות נזיקין?

steps.title: The number four rejects רבי אושעיא's thirteen
steps.stepSummary: The count of four comes to reject רבי אושעיא, who says there are thirteen main types of damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to reject רבי אושעיא, who says there are thirteen main categories of damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'four' is there to push away רבי אושעיא's bigger count of thirteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By fixing the number at four, the משנה shows it does not accept a list of thirteen. The count is a clear statement against the wider list.

keyTerms.meaning: Thirteen

phrases.english: To exclude the view of רבי אושעיא, who says:
There are thirteen main categories of damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number four rejects רבי אושעיא's count of thirteen.

steps.title: Why does רבי אושעיא give a number?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about רבי אושעיא: why does he say 'thirteen'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אושעיא, why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question on רבי אושעיא's own list of thirteen. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a number always has to reject something, then רבי אושעיא's thirteen must also be rejecting another view. The גמרא keeps climbing up the chain.

phrases.english: And according to רבי אושעיא, why do I need the number?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question to the opinion brought in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי אושעיא's count of thirteen reject?

steps.title: Thirteen rejects רבי חייא's twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא's thirteen comes to reject רבי חייא, who counts twenty-four main types of damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to reject רבי חייא, who says there are twenty-four main categories of damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אושעיא's number pushes away an even bigger list, רבי חייא's twenty-four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each list is longer than the one before it: four, then thirteen, then twenty-four. Each smaller count shows that its author does not accept the bigger list.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-four

phrases.english: To exclude the view of רבי חייא, who says:
There are twenty-four main categories of damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Thirteen rejects רבי חייא's count of twenty-four.

steps.title: Why does רבי חייא give a number?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks once more: according to רבי חייא, why say 'twenty-four'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי חייא, why do I need the number?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks its question one last time, now about the biggest list. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one has a bigger list than רבי חייא, so his number cannot be rejecting a bigger count. The answer will have to be something else.

phrases.english: And according to רבי חייא, why do I need the number?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question to רבי חייא's opinion from step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי חייא's count of twenty-four leave out?

steps.title: Twenty-four leaves out the informer and the one who makes a קרבן פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's number comes to leave out two kinds of damage: an informer, and someone who makes another person's קרבן פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude an informer and someone who makes a קרבן פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא's twenty-four is there to show that two cases are not on the list of main damages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the number does not reject a bigger count. It rules out specific cases: an informer who causes someone's property to be taken, and a כהן who makes someone's קרבן פיגול. These cases do cause loss, but they are not counted among the אבות נזיקין.

keyTerms.meaning: An informer who causes another person's property to be taken by the authorities
One who makes a קרבן פיגול through a wrong intention, so it becomes unfit

phrases.english: To exclude an informer and one who makes an offering פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 and closes the chain of 'why the number' questions about נזיקין.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number twenty-four leaves out an informer and one who makes a קרבן פיגול.
steps.whatToRemember: The chain goes four, then thirteen, then twenty-four. Each count rejects the bigger list after it. The last count, twenty-four, leaves out the informer and the one who makes a קרבן פיגול.

steps.title: Returning to the statement: liable for each one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the earlier teaching that one who did all the sins in one lapse of awareness is liable for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If he did all of them during one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a line it said earlier, so that it can examine it now. This step sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן explained that the משנה counts the 36 כריתות to teach something. Someone who did all of them in one הֶעְלֵם brings a separate קרבן for each. Now the גמרא will test whether that really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: One lapse of awareness: he did not realize in between that he was sinning
Liable for each and every one separately

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי יוחנן's explanation of why the משנה gives the number 36.

phrases.english: that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness –
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the counts of other תנאים and returns to the main teaching about the count of 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing all the כריתות in one הֶעְלֵם makes him liable for each one separately.

steps.title: Maybe all the forbidden relations count as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that since the פסוק lumps all the עריות together, doing them all in one lapse should bring only one liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, you cannot say he is completely exempt, since the פסוק says 'whoever does any of these abominations shall be cut off.' But maybe say: if he did one, he is liable for one, and if he did all of them in one lapse, he is liable for only one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from the last step for the עריות. It suggests that doing all of them in one lapse should be counted as just one sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק clearly makes the עריות punishable by כרת, so he cannot be fully exempt. But the same פסוק groups them all under one phrase, 'any of these abominations.' That grouping suggests they are one category, so one lapse would bring only one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted: we accept this part, but there is a problem with another part
Completely exempt
Abominations: here, the forbidden relations listed in the פרשה
Being cut off: the heavenly punishment for doing these sins on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the עריות are not punishable. It agrees they are. The only question is whether many of them in one lapse count as one sin or as many.

phrases.english: Granted, that he is completely exempt
you cannot say,
as it is written:
"For whoever shall do
any of these abominations, shall be cut off."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29

phrases.english: But say:
if he transgressed one, he became liable for one,
if he transgressed all of them in one lapse of awareness –
he is liable for only one!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא פָּטוּר לִגְמָרֵי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just quoted, as it applies to the עריות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that doing all of them in one הֶעְלֵם makes him liable for each one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק joins all the עריות in one phrase, which suggests they form one unit. Then one lapse should bring only one liability.

steps.title: The sister was singled out to split them up
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the תורה mentioned כרת separately for one's sister to teach that each ערוה is a separate liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: That is why כרת was stated separately for one's sister: to split them up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. He points to a פסוק that gives כרת to the sister on its own, even though she was already included in the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sister was already covered by the general כרת for all the עריות. So repeating כרת for her alone must teach something new. It teaches that the עריות are separate, so each one brings its own liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out: a case taken out of a general group and stated on its own
His sister
To divide: to show that the items count as separate liabilities

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for counting each ערוה separately. Because of it, someone who violated many in one lapse brings many חטאות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
For this reason כרת was singled out regarding his sister –
phrases.notes: The sister already appears in the general list, but ויקרא 20:17 gives her כרת again by itself.

phrases.english: to divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by bringing a פסוק that separates the עריות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a source from the extra mention of one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק groups the עריות together, they would count as one liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separate כרת for the sister shows that the עריות are divided, so each one is a separate liability.

steps.title: Maybe only the sister is separate
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי objects: maybe singling out the sister only makes her separate, while all the other עריות still count as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי objected: Say instead that for his sister, whom the פסוק listed separately, he is liable one on her own. But for all the others, since he did them in one lapse, he should be liable for only one!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי challenges רבי יוחנן's answer. He suggests a smaller conclusion from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the sister out of the group might only show that she is separate. It does not have to mean every ערוה is separate. Then the rest stay as one unit, and one lapse would bring just one extra liability for all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it: a later sage pushes back on a statement
The פסוק specified it: listed it separately

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye objected to this:
Say: his sister, whom the verse specified –
let him be liable for one on her account,
and all the rest, since they were in one lapse of awareness –
let him be liable for only one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks how far רבי יוחנן's source reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's proof that the separate כרת for the sister divides all the עריות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Singling out one case may separate only that case. Then the sister counts on her own, and the remaining עריות still count as one.

steps.title: Doesn't רב ביבי accept the rule about an item singled out from a group?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב ביבי בר אביי rejects a well-known ברייתא: an item singled out from a group teaches about the whole group.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב ביבי בר אביי, doesn't he accept what the ברייתא teaches: anything that was part of a group and was singled out to teach something was singled out to teach about the whole group, not only about itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ביבי's objection by quoting a famous rule of how to read the תורה. The rule says that when one item is pulled out of a group, its lesson applies to the entire group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ביבי claimed that singling out the sister only makes the sister separate. This rule says the opposite: the item singled out teaches about all the others too. So the sister should show that every ערוה is its own separate liability, just as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule or group that includes many items
Was singled out (taken out) from the general group
To teach a lesson about the entire group
Doesn't he hold / doesn't he accept?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about why the sister is singled out. It is a challenge to רב ביבי: the known rule says singling out spreads the lesson to the whole group, which would support רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Beivai bar Abaye,
does he not accept this, which is taught in a ברייתא:
Any matter that was included in a general group
and was singled out from the group to teach something,
was not singled out to teach about itself alone,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְלַמֵּד עַל הַכְּלָל כּוּלּוֹ יָצָא.
phrases.english: but was singled out to teach about the entire group.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי, מִי לֵית לֵיהּ הֲדָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ביבי's objection from step 31 using a known rule of reading the תורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי's claim that singling out the sister makes only the sister separate.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An accepted ברייתא says that an item singled out from a group teaches about the whole group. So the sister should teach that each ערוה is separate.

steps.title: The ברייתא's example: peace offerings teach about all altar offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows the rule using שלמים: they are singled out for כרת when eaten while impure, and that teaches the same law for all קדשי מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? 'And the soul that eats the flesh...' Weren't שלמים already included among all the holy offerings? Why were they singled out? To compare the others to them. Just as שלמים are holy for the altar and one is liable for them, so too one is liable for anything holy for the altar. This leaves out things that are holy for בדק הבית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא, which now gives an example to show how the rule works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names שלמים even though they already belong to the group of all offerings. The ברייתא says this is done to compare all altar offerings to שלמים, so eating any of them while impure brings כרת. Notice that the lesson reaches only items like שלמים, holy for the altar, and not קדשי בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings
To compare one thing to another so they share the same law (a היקש)
Things made holy to be brought on the altar
Things made holy for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: The last line, which leaves out קדשי בדק הבית, is exactly what רב ביבי will use in his answer.

phrases.english: How so?
"And the soul that eats the flesh, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:20. The פסוק goes on to speak about eating שלמים while impure, which brings כרת.

phrases.english: But weren't peace offerings already included among all the holy offerings?
Why were they singled out?
To compare the others to them:
Just as peace offerings, which are holy for the altar,
and one is liable for them,
phrases.notes: Liable to כרת for eating them while impure.

phrases.english: so too, anything that is holy for the altar,
one is liable for it,
which leaves out things holy for Temple upkeep!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא's example that shows the rule quoted in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: That an item singled out from a group teaches its law to the whole group.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on שלמים in ויקרא 7:20, which spreads כרת for eating while impure to all קדשי מזבח.

steps.title: רב ביבי: even there, not everything is included
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי answers that even in that ברייתא the lesson does not cover the whole group, since קדשי בדק הבית are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said to him: Leave that ברייתא aside. Didn't you say there that things holy for בדק הבית are left out?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי defends his objection. He points out that the very ברייתא quoted against him does not spread its lesson to everything in the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, singling out שלמים teaches only about items like them, and קדשי בדק הבית are left out. So singling out an item does not automatically teach about the entire group. In the same way, singling out the sister does not have to prove that every ערוה is separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave that aside; that is not a proof
Didn't you yourself say?
There, in that other case

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'יצא מן הכלל ללמד על הכלל כולו' has limits. Even in its main example, the lesson reaches only items like the one singled out, and קדשי בדק הבית are left out. רב ביבי uses this to defend his view that the sister does not have to teach about all the עריות.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai said to him:
Leave that aside.
Didn't you say there
that things holy for Temple upkeep are left out?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב בִּיבִי: בַּר מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 32 and 33 and defends רב ביבי's objection from step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule: the item singled out does not teach about the entire group without exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Singling out one item always spreads its lesson to every member of the group, so the sister teaches that each ערוה is separate.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the ברייתא's own example leaves out קדשי בדק הבית, so singling out the sister does not have to teach about all the עריות.

steps.title: Rav Beivai: maybe only women like the sister count separately
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי applies his point to our case. The sister can never become permitted to her brother, so maybe only עריות like her count separately, and אשת איש is left out because divorce can permit her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: just as a sister is special in that she is an ערוה who can never become permitted while the one who forbids her is alive, so too only a woman who can never become permitted while the one who forbids her is alive counts separately. That leaves out a married woman, who can become permitted while her husband is still alive!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי finishes his challenge to רבי יוחנן. Just as the שלמים lesson did not cover everything, the sister lesson may only cover עריות that are like the sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'one item singled out teaches about the group' only spreads to cases that share the special feature of that item. The sister's special feature is that she can never become permitted to her brother. אשת איש does not share that feature, since a divorce can permit her, so רבי יוחנן's teaching that every ערוה counts separately would not cover her.

keyTerms.meaning: Special, having a unique feature
A way to become permitted
While the person who makes her forbidden is still alive
A married woman

steps.confusionAlert: 'The one who forbids her' is not a בית דין. It means the relative who makes her forbidden: the brother for a sister, the husband for a married woman.

phrases.english: Here too:
just as his sister is special
in that she is a forbidden relative
and can never become permitted while the one who forbids her is alive,
phrases.notes: The 'one who forbids her' is her brother. She stays his sister his whole life.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶיתֵּר בְּחַיֵּי אוֹסְרָהּ,
phrases.english: so too, any woman who can never become permitted while the one who forbids her is alive,
this leaves out a married woman,
who can become permitted while her husband is still alive!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב ביבי's answer about the שלמים ברייתא (the lesson does not cover the whole group) back to the sister case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's derivation that the separate mention of כרת for the sister makes every ערוה a separate liability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lesson learned from a singled-out item only spreads to cases that share its special feature. The sister is never permitted to her brother, so אשת איש, who can become permitted through divorce, would not be included.

steps.title: The verse ties all the עריות to the sister through a הקש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה (some say רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע) answers that the פסוק 'כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבות' puts all the עריות together with the sister as a הקש. So every ערוה, אשת איש included, brings its own separate liability, just like the sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה said, and some say it was רב הונא the son of רב יהושע: The פסוק says, 'For whoever shall do any of these abominations.' Since the פסוק compares them this way, all the עריות are compared to the sister. Just as one is liable for the sister on her own, so too one is liable for each ערוה on her own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב ביבי's challenge and defends רבי יוחנן. The פסוק itself joins all the עריות to the sister, so there is no need to look for a special feature that matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ביבי's challenge only works if we learn from the sister by finding a shared feature. Here the פסוק makes a direct comparison (a הקש), which covers every ערוה in the list even if it is not like the sister in every way. So אשת איש is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: A direct comparison the תורה makes between two things, so they share the same law
They were compared (by the פסוק)
Abominations; here, the forbidden relations listed in the פרשה
On its own, as a separate liability

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the הקש ties all the עריות to the sister, so each ערוה brings its own separate liability, אשת איש included.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between a הקש and learning from a shared feature. A הקש does not need the cases to match in every detail.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yona said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua:
The verse says:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: "For whoever shall do any of these abominations, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29

phrases.english: since the verse compares them this way,
all the forbidden relations are compared to his sister:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֲחוֹתוֹ חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ,
phrases.english: just as one is liable for his sister on her own,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ.
phrases.english: so too, for each of them one is liable on her own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: כִּי כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ביבי's challenge in step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the learning method as a הקש, which does not need a shared special feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lesson spreads from the sister only to עריות that, like her, can never become permitted, so אשת איש is left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק directly compares all עריות to the sister, so each ערוה, אשת איש included, brings a separate liability.

steps.title: How does רבי יצחק know each ערוה counts separately?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק uses the extra mention of כרת for the sister for a different lesson: to punish with כרת and not מלקות. So the גמרא asks where he learns that each ערוה brings a separate liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יצחק, who says: all those who get כרת were already included in the general פסוק, and why was כרת for the sister mentioned on its own? To judge her case with כרת and not with מלקות. Where does he learn to count each one separately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a different תנא. It first states רבי יצחק's view to set up the question, and then asks where he learns that each ערוה is counted separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן learned the 'each one separately' rule from the extra mention of כרת for the sister. רבי יצחק already uses that same extra mention for a different lesson, about כרת instead of מלקות. So he cannot learn 'separate liability' from it, and he needs another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Sins that are punished with כרת
They were already included in the general statement
Lashes
To divide, meaning to count each sin as a separate liability
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yitzchak, who says:
those liable to כרת were all included in the general verse,
phrases.notes: The general verse is ויקרא 18:29, which gives כרת for all the עריות.

phrases.english: and why was כרת for his sister singled out?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:17

phrases.english: To judge her case with כרת and not with lashes,
from where does he learn to count each one separately?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּאָמַר: חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת בִּכְלָל הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled רבי יוחנן's source, the גמרא asks how רבי יצחק, who uses the same פסוק for something else, learns the same rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that each ערוה brings a separate liability, according to רבי יצחק

steps.title: רבי יצחק learns it from the פסוק about נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns from the words 'ואל אשה בנדת טומאתה לא תקרב' that one is liable separately for each and every woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'And to a woman in her impure state of נדה you shall not come near': this teaches to count separately for each and every woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. רבי יצחק has a different פסוק that teaches the 'separate liability' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק adds the word 'אשה' (a woman) when it talks about נדה. רבי יצחק reads this as teaching that each woman is her own separate liability. So he reaches the same rule as רבי יוחנן, just from a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it from
A woman who is impure because of her monthly period
Each and every woman

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יוחנן and רבי יצחק agree that each ערוה brings a separate liability. רבי יוחנן learns it from the sister and the הקש, and רבי יצחק learns it from the פסוק about נדה.

phrases.english: He learns it from: "And to a woman
in her impure state of נדה you shall not come near,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:19

phrases.english: to count separately for each and every woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״וְּאֶל אִשָּׁה בְּנִדַּת טוּמְאָתָהּ לֹא תִקְרַב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק learns the separate liability for each woman from the extra word 'אשה' in the פסוק about נדה (ויקרא 18:19).

steps.title: Why don't the רבנן also learn it from 'ואל אשה בנדת טומאתה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן: they could learn separate liability for each ערוה from רבי יצחק's פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן too: let them learn it from 'And to a woman in the separation of her טומאה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and asks why they need the sister's כרת to teach separate liability. They could learn it from the same פסוק רבי יצחק uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 38, רבי יצחק learned separate liability from 'ואל אשה בנדת טומאתה.' That פסוק is in the תורה for everyone, so the רבנן could use it too. If they did, the sister's extra כרת would no longer be needed for this lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them learn it from (a different source)
In the separation of her impurity, meaning a נדה

phrases.english: And the Rabbis too,
let them derive it
from "And to a woman in the separation of her impurity"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:19. This is the same פסוק רבי יצחק used in the last step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי יצחק's source from step 38 and asks why the רבנן don't use it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's use of the sister's כרת for separate liability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is already another פסוק that teaches the same thing, so the רבנן don't need the sister's כרת for it.

steps.title: Yes, the רבנן can learn it from there too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the רבנן can indeed learn separate liability from 'ואל אשה בנדת טומאתה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא simply agrees: the רבנן can learn it from that פסוק as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts the challenge instead of fighting it. This raises a new problem, because now the sister's extra כרת seems to have nothing left to teach for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (the גמרא accepts the point)

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 39.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן need the sister's כרת to teach separate liability for each ערוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן can learn separate liability from 'ואל אשה בנדת טומאתה,' just like רבי יצחק.

steps.title: Then what does the sister's כרת teach?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן learn from רבי יצחק's פסוק, the גמרא asks what the sister's extra כרת is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does the כרת of the sister come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the רבנן no longer need the sister's כרת for separate liability, the גמרא asks what that extra כרת is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה doesn't add words for nothing. רבי יצחק already uses the sister's כרת for 'כרת and not מלקות' (step 37). Now the גמרא needs a lesson for the רבנן's use of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The כרת mentioned separately for one's sister
What does it come to teach?

phrases.english: But the karet of his sister,
for what does it come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the concession in step 40, which left the sister's כרת without a job.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the רבנן learn from the extra כרת of the sister.

steps.title: To separate the sister, the father's sister and the mother's sister
steps.stepSummary: The sister's כרת teaches separate liability for one's sister, father's sister and mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed to separate the liability for his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sister's כרת teaches that one is liable separately for his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a first try at giving the sister's כרת a new lesson. It is about three related women, each counted separately. The next step will question whether this lesson is needed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To separate, meaning to require a separate חטאת for each
His father's sister (his aunt)
His mother's sister (his aunt)

phrases.english: It is needed to separate
for his sister,
and for his father's sister,
and for his mother's sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sister's כרת teaches separate liability for one's sister, father's sister and mother's sister.

steps.title: Three different women are obviously separate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: these are different prohibitions with different women, so obviously they are separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do these need a פסוק to separate them? They are separate names and separate bodies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that no פסוק is needed here. Three different women with three different names are obviously three separate sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A separate חטאת is obvious when both the prohibition's name and the person are different. Here both are different, so a פסוק teaching this would add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate names, meaning different categories of prohibition
Separate bodies, meaning different people

phrases.english: These, why do they need to be separated?
Behold, they are separate names,
and behold, they are separate bodies!
phrases.notes: He means three different women, so of course each one is a separate sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 42 as teaching something obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the sister's כרת separates the sister, father's sister and mother's sister
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different prohibitions done with different women are already obviously separate, so there is nothing for the פסוק to teach.

steps.title: One woman who is his sister, father's sister and mother's sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the answer: the lesson is about one woman who is all three relatives at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: to separate the liability for his sister who is also his father's sister and also his mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the answer. It is talking about one woman who is his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister all at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is only one woman and one act, but three names of prohibition. Without a פסוק we might think one act brings only one חטאת. The sister's כרת teaches that he brings three.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say it this way (the גמרא rewords the earlier statement)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not three women anymore. It is one single woman who is related to him in all three ways, which is why a פסוק is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, the sister's כרת teaches that one act with one woman who is his sister, father's sister and mother's sister brings three separate חטאות.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
to separate for his sister
who is his father's sister
and who is his mother's sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the answer of step 42 so it is no longer obvious, answering step 43.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lesson was about three different women.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lesson is about one woman who is all three relatives, and he brings three חטאות for one act.

steps.title: Where does רבי יצחק learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יצחק learns the lesson of one woman who is all three relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק, from where does he learn this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק uses the sister's כרת for 'כרת and not מלקות,' so the גמרא asks where he learns the three-חטאות lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides seem to agree on the law of the woman who is all three relatives. The sister's כרת is already busy for רבי יצחק, so he needs another source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn this matter?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak,
this matter, from where does he have it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the lesson of step 44 and asks for רבי יצחק's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יצחק's source for three חטאות for a woman who is his sister, father's sister and mother's sister.

steps.title: From the end of the פסוק: 'ערות אחתו גלה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns it from the extra words at the end of the פסוק, 'ערות אחתו גלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the end of the פסוק, as it is written: 'He has uncovered his sister's nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק learns it from the end of the same פסוק, which mentions the sister again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already spoke about the sister, so repeating 'ערות אחתו גלה' looks extra. רבי יצחק uses those extra words for the three-חטאות lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the פסוק
He has uncovered his sister's nakedness

phrases.english: He derives it
from the end of the verse,
as it is written: "He has uncovered his sister's nakedness."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק learns it from the extra words 'ערות אחתו גלה' at the end of the פסוק.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with 'אחתו' at the end of the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the extra word 'אחתו' at the end of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with 'his sister' at the end of the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן learn the three-חטאות lesson from the sister's כרת, so the גמרא asks what they learn from the extra 'אחתו.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra word must teach something. The רבנן don't need 'ערות אחתו גלה' for the three-חטאות lesson, so it needs its own job for them.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (what do they learn from it)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
